checks: For positive source depth, set R to its dth root. The independent-array predecessor gives R≤min_i |K_i|^(1/d) and the directional quantile threshold inequality for every allocation with sum α_i^d=1, including the exact full-source endpoint.

Zero quantile allocation corresponds to a nonempty supporting face, full allocation to the whole source. Their convex Minkowski combination is therefore valid in Brunn–Minkowski and lies in the through-mark ordinary cap by the weighted threshold inequality.

Maximizing the linear sum of λ_i α_i on the positive ℓ_d unit sphere yields the dual norm for d>1 and max λ_i for d=1. Raising to the dth power gives (sum λ_i^(d/(d−1)))^(d−1). Equal λ_i give 1/N in both cases. The zero-depth case is automatic.
Read 239caf8af54c6294 §9, (18)–(19). Taking the infimum of through-mark ordinary caps is the ordinary raw depth because tightening parallel to the mark can only remove volume.
